incidents.cause: The failure of the pilot receiving instruction to adequately compensate for the crosswind condition and failure to maintain directional control.  Also causal was the flight instructor's delayed remedial action and inadequate supervision of the flight.
The pilot's excessive speed and excessive application of brakes during the landing roll on soft, sandy terrain.
The pilot's selection of unsuitable terrain for landing.
The pilot's incorrect brake application during the landing roll, which resulted in a nose over.
